findings.text: blocking: the graph-closure judgment member is built by _judgment_member(graph_project, graph_slug, dependency[1], judgment), which qualifies BOTH the dependent and the target with graph_project. When the blocking dependency is in another mounted project - the case resolve_graph_target exists to serve - the target ref names the dependent's project, not the dependency's, so the member names a plan that does not exist. Reproduced: alpha's endpoint depends_on beta:base, beta:base all-deferred -> judgment_required.members[0].target == "alpha:base" where the dependency's own ref is "beta:base"; the same-project control reports the correct "proj:G". _qualified_plan(target_project, dependency[1]) is needed, and _judgment_member's single-project signature cannot express it.

follow-on: judgment_required carries its count under the key count where the schedule_override block section 9 says it mirrors carries it under deferred, so the two blocks are not the identical shape the plan names; the run declined the rename with a rationale, so this is the coordinator's call, not a defect this review resolves.
